A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, Algorithm 1, and central convergence theorem. All pages, including appendices and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports original simulations of a stochastic convex toy problem, examining convergence under different weight-decay values.

after.justification: The toy simulations are retained, and Appendix E adds original GPT-2 training diagnostics on OpenWebText.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 is unchanged, including momentum, preconditioner updates, tunable exponents, and decoupled weight decay. The GPT-2 experiments apply the existing optimizer.

E1.justification: v2 adds GPT-2 pretraining on OpenWebText, extending empirical coverage from the retained synthetic matrix optimization problem to Transformer language-model training.

E2.justification: Neither version reports original comparisons against competing optimizers. Appendix E.1 attributes optimizer comparisons to other papers; AdamW handles remaining GPT-2 parameters within the training setup and is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a GPT-2 Small protocol with 10,000 training steps, batch size 640, warmup and cosine scheduling, gradient clipping, and alternating training/logging phases to approximate full gradients. The existing toy protocol is retained.

E4.justification: New diagnostics examine the nuclear-to-Frobenius gradient-norm ratio and preconditioner spectral floors relative to noise and regularization scales across four parameter classes. These directly investigate the theory's practical applicability; the original weight-decay sensitivity experiment remains.

E5.justification: Appendix E introduces an approximate stochastic-gradient-noise variance estimator using mini-batch deviations from an accumulated large-batch gradient. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 add gradient-ratio, minimum-eigenvalue, and estimated noise-scale trajectories for GPT-2. Figure 2 shows ratios rising late in training beneath the 27.713 reference. Figure 1's toy-result curves and weight-decay findings are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1 and its main proof are retained. Remark 3.7 adds a derivation relaxing the moment-parameter restriction from beta <= sqrt(theta) to beta <= theta^(1/128), with larger constants. Auxiliary matrix inequalities gain semidefinite coverage, and Gaussian variance statements are corrected.

C1.justification: The convergence-rate and unification claims remain. Section 1.1 newly claims empirical validation of the ideal gradient-norm regime on GPT-2, while the abstract and conclusion make the balanced-dimension qualification explicit.

C2.justification: v2 adds a signal-to-total-energy interpretation connecting Shampoo to Muon, a conjecture that the dimensional factor is unavoidable, and interpretations of the GPT-2 diagnostics. It also explicitly acknowledges that the weight-decay upper bound's tightness is unknown.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds model architecture, optimizer hyperparameters, scheduling, batch size, clipping, parameter allocation, logging procedures, eight-H200 hardware information, and a code-availability link. The retained toy experiment newly specifies p = q = 2; this is additional disclosure.

R1.justification: New Appendix A positions Shampoo within preconditioned non-Euclidean steepest descent and compares its theory with Gratton and Toint. Section 2 adds AdaGrad lower-bound and Muon/SignSGD connections. Publication updates to existing references, including Xie et al., are not new works.

P1.justification: The existing argument and proof structure are largely preserved. v2 refines terminology and notation, reorders parts of Section 2, restates the existing iterate bound as Lemma 3.8, and inserts appendices that shift the former A–C material to B–D.

P2.justification: v2 adds two four-panel figures displaying the new gradient-ratio and spectral/noise diagnostics. Figure 1 is relocated with its plots retained. The additions substantially expand the visual evidence without adding tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the assessment of practical relevance through original GPT-2 diagnostics, detailed implementation information, and clearer mathematical qualifications. The gains are useful but limited: the central theorem remains unchanged, and approximate gradients and noise estimates from one training setup do not establish dimensional scaling or satisfaction of all theorem conditions.
